# Overview of workers

Workers are primarily used as network proxies for Boundary sessions that allow you to access private targets. Instead of exposing a private network to the public or allowing users to have access to entire private networks, workers create a direct network tunnel between users and targets.

Workers are services that can run on a container or virtual machine. You should deploy them strategically within networks to provide access to targets.
In all editions of Boundary, workers are fully self-managed and can be deployed anywhere.
In HCP Boundary, HCP-managed workers are automatically deployed with the cluster.

All workers within Boundary use certificates and encryption keys to identify
themselves and protect data in transit. You can register workers using controller-led, worker-led, or external KMS workflows to fit your needs.

You must register workers using the worker-led or controller-led methods in the system with an API call. These workers require storage on-disk to store the current set of credentials. Workers using an external KMS auto-register after authenticating. This makes KMS an easy mechanism to use for automatic scaling.
KMS registration also does not require workers to store credentials locally; the KMS re-authenticates them each time they connect.

## Deploy a worker

Deploying a worker follows the same sequence regardless of which edition of Boundary you run:

1. [Create the worker configuration](/boundary/docs/workers/create) file that defines the listener, the upstream, and any tags.
1. [Start the worker](/boundary/docs/workers/start) and confirm that it reaches its upstream.
1. [Register the worker](/boundary/docs/workers/registration) with a controller using the method that fits your workflow.
1. [Add worker tags](/boundary/docs/workers/worker-tags) and [configure worker filters](/boundary/docs/workers/filters) to control which sessions the worker proxies. You can tag workers when you create the worker configuration file or after you have deployed them.

After the worker runs, refer to [Manage workers](/boundary/docs/workers/manage) for the operations you perform over its lifetime, and to [Troubleshoot workers](/boundary/docs/workers/troubleshoot) when something does not work as expected.

The pages in this section describe how to configure and operate an individual worker.
Refer to the following topics if you want to deploy a full environment or a fleet of workers:

- [Deploy workers](/boundary/docs/deploy/self-managed/deploy-workers) for the self-managed deployment procedure, including environment files, KMS key preparation, and systemd.
- [Deploy workers using a Helm chart](/boundary/docs/deploy/helm-chart/deploy-worker) to run workers on Kubernetes.
- [System requirements](/boundary/docs/architecture/system-requirements) for hardware sizing and network connectivity requirements.

## Session recording

Session recording requires at least one worker with access to local and remote storage.
Workers used for session recording require an accessible directory defined by `recording_storage_path` for storing in-progress session recordings. On session closure, a local session recording is moved to remote storage and deleted locally.

The `recording_storage_minimum_available_capacity` value determines the minimum amount of storage space that is required for workers to perform session recording operations. If a worker is at or below the storage threshold, Boundary does not use the worker to record sessions or play back recordings.

Development example:

```hcl
worker {
  auth_storage_path="/var/lib/boundary"
  initial_upstreams = ["10.0.0.1"]
  recording_storage_path="/local/storage/directory"
  recording_storage_minimum_available_capacity="500MB"
}
```
